11-04.q: Is your current 'vigilance' focused on your own soul, or are you too busy watching the faults of others?

saint.text: Truth is the property of no individual but is the treasure of all.

11-05.q: What 'shifting sand' are you standing on right now that needs to be replaced by the 'Rock' of Christ?

saint.text: We should always give thanks to God for everything that happens to us.

11-06.q: Are you living as a witness of God's 'enduring truth' for the next generation, or are you following the trends of today?

saint.text: God is the only light that can dispel the darkness of the grave.

11-07.q: Do you fear the future, or do you trust that you are securely held in 'the hand of God'?

saint.text: The higher we go, the better we shall hear the voice of Christ.

11-08.q: Has your light 'increased' this year, or has the world dimmed your fervor for the Gospel?

saint.text: Our hearts are the real temples of the Holy Spirit.

11-09.q: If your body is a 'temple,' what activities or thoughts have you allowed inside that desecrate it?

saint.text: The shepherd should be approachable to all, yet firm in the truth.

11-10.q: Are you 'firm in the truth' when it is unpopular, or do you stay quiet to avoid social friction?

saint.text: Lord, if your people still need me, I do not draw back from the labor.

11-11.q: In what small way can you 'clothe the naked' today, perhaps by protecting someone's reputation from gossip?

saint.text: Unity in the Church is the greatest strength of the faithful.

11-12.q: When was the last time you brought a 'contrite heart' to the Sacrament of Reconciliation?

saint.text: The poor are the representatives of Christ; to serve them is to serve Him.

11-13.q: Are you investing more time in your 'lasting city' in Heaven or your temporary home on Earth?

saint.text: Prayer is the wings by which the soul flies to God.

11-14.q: What 'gift' from today can you trace back to God's providence rather than your own hard work?

saint.text: Knowledge without love only puffeth up; but love edifieth.

11-15.q: Are you using your intelligence to serve others, or to make yourself feel superior?

saint.text: A soul that loves God finds its peace even in the midst of trials.

11-16.q: Is your peace currently dependent on your circumstances, or on your union with Christ?

saint.text: We should use the things of this world as if we used them not.

11-17.q: If everything you owned was taken away today, would your identity in Christ remain unshaken?

saint.text: Faith is the foundation of all that we do.

11-18.q: Has your charity 'increased' toward the person you find most difficult to be around?

saint.text: True nobility is found in the service of God.

11-19.q: Are your words today building up (edifying) those around you, or are they tearing them down?

saint.text: Humility is the only ladder that reaches to heaven.

11-20.q: In what way is God being a 'shield' for you today by closing a door that was dangerous for your soul?

saint.text: Mary offered herself to God in the temple, and so should we.

11-21.q: How can you 'present' your daily work to God today as a holy offering?

saint.text: To sing is to pray twice.

11-22.q: Is there a 'song of praise' in your heart today, or only a list of complaints?

saint.text: The soul's salvation is the only thing that matters.

11-23.q: Is there a specific 'gate' of your heart that you have kept locked because you fear Christ's light?

saint.text: A martyr's blood is the seed of the Church.

11-24.q: Are you willing to 'suffer' small social inconveniences for the sake of the 'Light of Life'?

saint.text: Faith is the light that guides us through the darkness of this world.

11-25.q: Do you treat your coworkers and employees with the 'justice' that you would want from God?

saint.text: The more we give to God, the more He gives to us.

11-26.q: Where is your 'own prudence' causing you anxiety because you haven't yet trusted the Lord with the outcome?

saint.text: Mary is the source of all our hope.
saint.who: Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal

11-27.q: Do you pray with the confidence that God is actively 'listening' to you right now?

saint.text: Patience is the only way to conquer the world.

11-28.q: What 'spiritual debris' has built up in your heart this month that needs to be cleared out?

saint.text: Let us always be prepared to meet the Lord.

11-29.q: If Christ came for your soul tonight, would you be 'ready' or would you be ashamed of how you spent today?

saint.text: To follow Christ is the only path to true joy.

11-30.q: As November ends, who in your life is waiting for you to 'cast a net' of faith and invite them to Christ?

saint.text: Advent is a time of waiting for the Light to enter our darkness.

12-01.q: In the 'darkness' of your current struggles, are you looking for a worldly solution or for the 'Rain' of the Just One?

saint.text: A soul that is at peace with God is a soul that is ready for anything.

12-02.q: Is your heart 'at peace' today, or are you letting the 'iniquity' of the world disturb your internal silence?

saint.text: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world and suffer the loss of his own soul?
saint.work: Letters to the Society of Jesus

12-03.q: Are you more concerned with 'gaining the world' (status and wealth) or with the health of your soul?

saint.text: The Son of God became man so that we might become God.

12-04.q: Does the reality of 'God with us' (Emmanuel) change the way you face loneliness today?

saint.text: Prayer is the best preparation for the coming of the King.

12-05.q: Are you using this season to 'prepare' your heart, or are you just busy with the 'preparations' of the world?

saint.text: The giver of every good gift is the Lord Himself.

12-06.q: When you give to others today, are you doing it to be seen, or to reflect the 'secret' generosity of God?

saint.text: The Church is the ship in which we sail safely through the storms of life.

12-07.q: Is there a 'storm' in your life right now where you have forgotten that Christ is the Captain of the ship?

saint.text: Mary is the most beautiful flower that has ever bloomed in the garden of God.

12-08.q: How can you honor the 'purity' of Mary today in your own thoughts and conversations?

saint.text: Am I not here, who am your Mother? Are you not under my shadow and protection?
saint.who: St. Juan Diego (Words of Our Lady)

12-09.q: Do you feel 'under the shadow' of Mary's protection, or are you trying to solve your problems entirely on your own?

saint.text: Our Lady of Loreto is the house where the Word became Flesh.

12-10.q: Is your home a place where the 'Word' can dwell, or is it filled with the noise of distraction?

saint.text: The shepherd of the Church must be a defender of the faith.

12-11.q: Are you 'defending' your faith in your social circles, or are you hiding it to fit in?

saint.text: I am the Mother of the true God for Whom one lives.

12-12.q: Do you live as if you are truly 'living for God,' or are you just surviving for yourself?

saint.text: To die for the faith is to find the true light.

12-13.q: Is there a 'darkness' in your life (envy, pride, or fear) that you have not yet allowed the Light of Christ to enter?

saint.text: In the evening of life, we will be judged on love alone.

12-14.q: If you were 'judged on love' today, would you be satisfied with the way you treated the people closest to you?

saint.text: Silence is the guardian of the spiritual life.

12-15.q: Can you find ten minutes of 'silence' today to simply listen for the Shepherd's voice?

saint.text: Every soul that loves is a soul that prays.

12-16.q: Is your prayer life 'going forwards,' or have you stopped growing in your relationship with God?

saint.text: The wisdom of the world is a heavy burden, but the wisdom of God is a light yoke.

12-17.q: Are you seeking 'prudence' (the right way to act) through prayer, or through the opinions of the world?

saint.text: Let us prepare the way of the Lord in our souls.

12-18.q: What ' Bethlehem'—small, humble, and overlooked—is God using to work a miracle in your life right now?

saint.text: The heart of a Christian should be a dwelling place for God.

12-19.q: If Christ were to be born in your 'heart' tonight, would He find it 'clean' and ready for Him?

saint.text: Mary's 'Yes' is the key that opened the door to our salvation.

12-20.q: In what specific area of your life is God waiting for your 'Yes'—your total surrender?

saint.text: Blessed is the one who believes in the promises of the Lord.

12-21.q: Do you 'believe' God's promises even when your current situation seems to contradict them?

saint.text: True joy is not found in things, but in the presence of God.

12-22.q: Is your soul 'magnifying' (making bigger) the goodness of God today, or the problems you are facing?

saint.text: Silence is the language of God; all else is a poor translation.

12-23.q: Are you 'preparing the way' for Christ in your home, or are you too busy with the noise of the holidays?

saint.text: Tonight, Heaven and Earth are joined in the Person of a Child.

12-24.q: As you stand at the threshold of Christmas, what is the one 'gift' of your heart you want to give to the Christ Child?

saint.text: Awake, O man! For your sake God became man.

12-25.q: How does the fact that 'God became man' change the way you see the dignity of every person you meet today?

saint.text: The first martyr is the seed of the Church's courage.

12-26.q: Are you 'looking up' toward Heaven when you are faced with criticism, or are you looking for an earthly defense?

saint.text: God is love, and he that abideth in love, abideth in God.

12-27.q: Is the 'love' you show others today a reflection of the 'Love' that is God?

saint.text: The innocent suffer, but their blood is not shed in vain.

12-28.q: How are you protecting the 'innocence' of your own soul and the souls of the children in your life?

saint.text: I die for the Name of Jesus and for the defense of the Church.

12-29.q: Are you 'edifying' your community, or are your words contributing to its division?

saint.text: Let us always be ready to serve the Lord with all our hearts.

12-30.q: As the year draws to a close, can you see how God's 'eyes' have been upon you through every trial?

saint.text: The time of life is short; let us use it for the glory of God.

12-31.q: As you stand at the end of this year, are you ready to meet the Son of Man today?

saint.text: But of this let us take heed, namely, that our soul herself sleep not: for evil is the sleep of the soul.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Expositions on the Psalms

advent-1.q: Where has your soul grown drowsy this year? Name one habit of prayer or attention you will wake up to before this week ends.

saint.text: Let no man then of them that live in vice despair; let no man who lives in virtue slumber.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew

advent-2.q: Are you tempted to drift because life feels easy, or to despair because it feels hard? Choose one concrete way to stay awake today.

saint.text: As we have opportunity, let us help on our salvation, let us get oil for our lamps, let us labor to add to our talent.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew

advent-3.q: What is the oil your lamp needs: prayer, mercy, patience? Decide today one small act to add to it.

saint.text: Let us then imitate them, and not quench our lamps, but keep them bright by alms-doing, for so is the light of this fire preserved.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on John

advent-4.q: Which almsgiving or kindness keeps your light burning? Choose one person to help this week so your lamp stays bright.

saint.text: Let us sing unto the Lord in our life. Our life at present is only hope; our life will be eternity hereafter
saint.who: St. Augustine, Expositions on the Psalms

advent-5.q: Where do you need to hold your hope more loosely than your plans? Name one thing you will wait on God for this Advent.

saint.text: Thou awakest us to delight in Thy praise; for Thou madest us for Thyself, and our heart is restless, until it repose in Thee.

advent-6.q: Which restlessness in you is really a longing for God? Set aside ten quiet minutes today and offer that restlessness to Him.

saint.text: Lo, He hath not yet come: He is in heaven, thou on earth: He delayeth His coming, do not thou delay wisdom.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Expositions on the Psalms

advent-7.q: The Lord delays His coming, but not your growth. What one wise decision have you been postponing that you can make today?

saint.text: Thou seest that it is good to make confession. Thou seest that there is salvation for them that repent.
saint.who: St. Cyril of Jerusalem, Catechetical Lectures

advent-8.q: What sin have you been avoiding naming? Make a confession this week, trusting that salvation, not condemnation, waits on the other side.

saint.text: For man’s confession is man’s lowliness: God’s pity is God’s loftiness. Therefore, since He came to forgive man his sins, let man acknowledge his own lowliness and let God show His pity.

advent-9.q: Where must a mountain of pride be lowered in you? Tell God one thing plainly, and let Him fill the valley with mercy.

saint.text: At the Word and the Voice my thought marvelled:—for lo! John was the Voice;—our Lord was manifested as the Word, that what was hidden should become revealed.
saint.who: St. Ephrem the Syrian, Hymns on the Nativity

advent-10.q: John was only a voice pointing to the Word. Whom could you point toward Christ this week, with one honest, humble word?

saint.text: Before the Lord Jesus came, men were glorying of themselves; He came a man, to lessen man’s glory, and to increase the glory of God.

advent-11.q: Where do you still glory in yourself? Choose one accomplishment today and quietly give the credit to God.

saint.text: Forego vengeance, forgive offences: exchange severity for gentleness, indignation for meekness, discord for peace.

advent-12.q: Which rough place between you and another needs smoothing? Make one concrete exchange today: a kind word, a forgiven debt, an apology.

saint.text: Therefore, knowing these things, let us use great diligence, while we are in the threshing floor; for it is possible while we are here, to change even out of chaff into wheat, even as on the other hand many from wheat have become chaff.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew

advent-13.q: Chaff can become wheat only while we are still on the threshing floor. What one change will you begin today, not later?

saint.text: For it is God’s part to give a contrite and humbled heart, sober, self-possessed, and awestruck, full of repentance and compunction.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew

advent-14.q: Ask God for a contrite heart rather than manufacturing one. What sorrow, honestly named in prayer today, might He be asking you to hand over?

saint.text: Let the saint exult in that he draws near to victory. Let the sinner be glad in that he is invited to pardon. Let the gentile take courage in that he is called to life.

advent-15.q: Which of the three describes you today: the saint, the sinner, the stranger? Receive that invitation, then share your gladness with one person.

saint.text: Let us not therefore despair, but having so many motives and good hopes, though we sin every day, let us approach Him, entreating, beseeching, asking the forgiveness of our sins.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew

advent-16.q: What failure keeps you from approaching God? Take it to Him in prayer today, and receive His strength before you try again.

saint.text: She, when the angel entered, was found at home in privacy, without a companion, that no one might interrupt her attention or disturb her; and she did not desire any women as companions, who had the companionship of good thoughts.

advent-17.q: Mary was found in quiet when the angel came. Where will you make room for silence today so that God can find you at home?

saint.text: Of what handmaid? Her who when He was announced as about to be born of her, answered and said, “Behold the handmaid of the Lord: be it unto me according to Thy word.”
saint.who: St. Augustine, Expositions on the Psalms

advent-18.q: Mary said yes before she understood. What is one thing God is asking of you that you can agree to today without all the answers?

saint.text: For she became more humble when she knew herself to be chosen of God, and went forthwith to her kinswoman in the hill country, not in order to gain belief by anything external, for she had believed the word of God.

advent-19.q: Mary hurried to serve after being honored. Whom could you go to help this week, setting aside any sense of being special?

saint.text: Magnify Him truly, magnify Him well. Let us praise Him, let us magnify Him who hath wrought the very righteousness which we have; who wrought it in us, Himself.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Expositions on the Psalms

advent-20.q: Mary’s praise names God as the doer of good. Write down three good things in you that He worked, and thank Him for each.

saint.text: The day that Gabriel came in unto my low estate, he made me free instead of a handmaid, of a sudden: for I was the handmaid of Thy Divine Nature, and am also the Mother of Thy human Nature, O Lord and Son!
saint.who: St. Ephrem the Syrian, Hymns on the Nativity

advent-21.q: God looked on Mary’s lowliness and raised her. What do you consider too small or poor in yourself to offer Him this Advent?

saint.text: When man’s hope had broken down, hope was increased by Thy Birth.
saint.who: St. Ephrem the Syrian, Hymns on the Nativity

advent-22.q: Hope breaks down in every life. Where has yours broken, and how will you let the coming of Christ restore it this week?

saint.text: What is so new as to be born of a virgin? Therefore, because there was not in Him what instruction might renew, because He had no sin, there was given Him a new origin of birth.

advent-23.q: Christ comes as a gift, not as an achievement of ours. What do you need to receive from God this week rather than try to earn?

saint.text: I was jealous of Thy Mother, and I thought to put her away, and I knew not that in her womb was hidden a mighty treasure, that should suddenly enrich my poor estate.
saint.who: St. Ephrem the Syrian, Hymns on the Nativity

advent-24.q: Joseph misjudged what God was doing. Where might you be misreading a hidden good in your own life? Ask God to show it to you.

saint.text: Again, when thou seest Him lying in a manger, thou wilt not be anxious to put golden garments about thy child, or to cause thy wife’s couch to be inlaid with silver.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on John

advent-25.q: The King chose a manger. What excess in your Christmas preparations can you trim, and give the saving to someone who has little?

saint.text: That unfailing Light, the Light of wisdom, speaking through the cloud of the flesh, says to men, “I am the light of the world; he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.”

advent-26.q: What part of your life still walks in darkness? Bring it to Christ today and follow Him one honest step into the light.

saint.text: We know in what consulship the Virgin Mary brought forth Christ, conceived of the Holy Ghost. Wherefore He, by whom as God the times were made, was made man in time.

advent-27.q: God entered time at the fullness of time. What are you hurrying through, or putting off, that you could live more attentively this very day?

saint.text: First, then, no one ought to be ashamed of becoming poor after being rich, if this happens because he gives freely to the poor; for Christ became poor when He was rich, that through His poverty He might enrich all.
saint.who: St. Ambrose, On the Duties of the Clergy

advent-28.q: Christ became poor for you. What generous gift, of money, time or forgiveness, will you give away before Christmas so someone else is enriched?

saint.text: So likewise the Wisdom of God, the Word of God, the Lord Jesus Christ, is everywhere present, because the truth is everywhere, wisdom is everywhere.

dec-17.q: O Wisdom, ordering all things: where in your ordinary day have you overlooked God’s quiet presence? Pause three times today to notice it.

saint.text: For to examine into the testimonies of the Lord, and to seek Him with all the heart, this is to be undefiled in the way, this is to walk in the law of the Lord.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Expositions on the Psalms

dec-18.q: O Lord and Lawgiver: which commandment do you treat as a burden rather than a path? Seek Him in it with your whole heart today.

saint.text: For our root is Christ, who hath ascended into heaven. Humbled, he shall be exalted; “he shall spread abroad like a cedar in Libanus.”
saint.who: St. Augustine, Expositions on the Psalms

dec-19.q: O Root of Jesse, from whom you draw life: what keeps you from staying rooted in Him? Take one practical step today to be nourished.

saint.text: Blessed be the Merciful One, who saw the weapon by Paradise, that closed the way to the Tree of Life; and came and took a Body which could suffer, that with the Door, that was in His side, He might open the way into Paradise.
saint.who: St. Ephrem the Syrian, Hymns on the Nativity

dec-20.q: O Key of David, who opens what no one can shut: which locked door in your life will you ask Him to open today?

saint.text: Thou flashedst, shonest, and scatteredst my blindness. Thou breathedst odours, and I drew in breath and panted for Thee. I tasted, and hunger and thirst. Thou touchedst me, and I burned for Thy peace.

dec-21.q: O Rising Dawn: where has His light scattered your blindness? Name one thing you now see clearly, and thank Him for the light before dark.

saint.text: For the kingdom is the Lord’s, not proud men’s: and He shall rule over the nations.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Expositions on the Psalms

dec-22.q: O King of the nations: what part of your life still resists His rule? Give Him that area this evening, and pray for the nations.

saint.text: The Word of God was made flesh by the dispensation of the Virgin, to abolish death and make man live.
saint.who: St. Irenaeus, Demonstration of the Apostolic Preaching

dec-23.q: O Emmanuel, God with us in flesh: where do you most need Him near? Speak that need aloud to Him tonight, and trust He has come.

saint.text: There is for all one common measure of joy, because as our Lord the destroyer of sin and death finds none free from charge, so is He come to free us all.

dec-24.q: Tonight the long waiting ends. Who is still outside your joy, unforgiven or forgotten? Reach out to that one person before the feast begins.

saint.text: Our Saviour, dearly-beloved, was born today: let us be glad. For there is no proper place for sadness, when we keep the birthday of the Life, which destroys the fear of mortality and brings to us the joy of promised eternity.
saint.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on the Nativity

dec-25.q: Where in your day will you let joy, not worry, have the last word, because the Saviour has been born for you?

saint.text: By the death of martyrs religion has been defended, faith increased, the Church strengthened; the dead have conquered, the persecutors have been overcome.
saint.who: St. Ambrose, On the Belief in the Resurrection

dec-26.q: Stephen forgave the very people stoning him. Whose wrong against you could you release today, praying for that person by name?

saint.text: If, therefore, God gave to thee grace, because He gave freely, love freely. Do not for the sake of reward love God; let Him be the reward.

dec-27.q: God loved you first and freely. Whom can you love today with no expectation of return, simply because you were loved?

saint.text: The Lord desired that we should rejoice and leap for joy in persecutions, because, when persecutions occur, then are given the crowns of faith, then the soldiers of God are proved, then the heavens are opened to martyrs.
saint.who: St. Cyprian, Letter to the People of Thibaris

dec-28.q: Rachel weeps while heaven opens to the little ones. For whom are you tempted to despair, and how could you entrust them to God today?

saint.text: It is not necessary for being with God to be always at church; we may make an oratory of our heart, wherein to retire from time to time, to converse with Him in meekness, humility, and love.
saint.who: Brother Lawrence, The Practice of the Presence of God

dec-29.q: Simeon met Christ because he was led into the Temple. What small, quiet place in your day could become your own oratory of the heart?

saint.text: He takes a body of our Nature, and that of a spotless Virgin, in whose womb He makes it His own, wherein to reveal Himself, conquer death, and restore life.
saint.who: St. Athanasius, On the Incarnation of the Word

dec-30.q: God took a body to give you life. What part of your ordinary, bodily life can you offer to Him today?

saint.text: Thou awakest us to delight in Thy praise; for Thou madest us for Thyself, and our heart is restless, until it repose in Thee.

dec-31.q: Looking back over this year, what is one gift you can name aloud in praise before the year closes?

saint.text: Therefore, to say, “they shall call” Him “Emmanuel,” means nothing else than that they shall see God amongst men.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew

jan-02.q: Emmanuel means God is with us. Where this week do you need to notice His presence among people rather than seek Him elsewhere?

saint.text: But because “the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us,” by His very nativity he made an eye-salve to cleanse the eyes of our heart, and to enable us to see His majesty by means of His humility.

jan-03.q: The Word became flesh in humility. Which humble, ordinary thing in front of you can help clear your eyes to see His majesty?

saint.text: And just as through a disobedient virgin man was stricken down and fell into death, so through the Virgin who was obedient to the Word of God man was reanimated and received life.
saint.who: St. Irenaeus, Demonstration of the Apostolic Preaching

jan-04.q: Mary pondered and obeyed. What word of God have you heard lately, and what one obedient step could you take on it today?

saint.text: For the unwonted splendour of a bright new star appeared to the wise men and filled their mind with such wonder, as they gazed upon its brilliance, that they could not think they ought to neglect what was announced to them with such distinctness.
saint.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on the Epiphany

jan-05.q: The Magi followed a sign they could have ignored. What nudge toward God have you been neglecting that you could follow this week?

saint.text: If those men journeyed so far to see Him newly born, what sort of excuse wilt thou have, not going out of thy way one alley’s length, that thou mayest visit Him sick or in bonds?
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew

jan-06.q: The Magi travelled far to worship. Whom could you visit this week, the sick or lonely, as a gift offered to Christ?

saint.text: With the servants the Lord, with the criminals the Judge, cometh to be baptized. But be not thou troubled; for in these humiliations His exaltation doth most shine forth.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew

jan-07.q: Jesus stood among sinners in humility. Where might you step down from being right or important and stand alongside someone today?

saint.text: Wherefore were the heavens opened? To inform thee that at thy baptism also this is done, God calling thee to thy country on high, and persuading thee to have nothing to do with earth.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew

jan-08.q: The heavens opened at Jesus’ baptism and at yours. What earthly attachment could you loosen today to hear the call to your heavenly home?

saint.text: They heard that “He taketh away the sin of the world,” and straightway they ran to Him.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on John

jan-09.q: Hearing that He takes away sin, people ran to Him. What sin or burden will you bring to Him in confession or prayer today?

saint.text: The dove is that in the form of which the Holy Spirit descended, as you have read in the New Testament, Who inspires in you peace of soul and tranquillity of mind.

jan-10.q: The Spirit came as a gentle dove. Where could you answer a sharp word with peace and a calm mind today?

saint.text: The mystery of this boon is great, dearly beloved, and this gift exceeds all gifts that God should call man son, and man should name God Father: for by these terms we perceive and learn the love which reached so great a height.
saint.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on the Nativity

jan-11.q: You are called a child of God. What would change in how you speak to Him this week if you prayed as a beloved son or daughter?

saint.text: For He is the same God who, throughout the whole creation, worketh miracles every day, which become lightly esteemed by men, not because of the ease with which they are wrought, but by reason of their constant recurrence.

jan-12.q: We grow used to miracles that happen every day. What ordinary gift, such as food, health or friendship, will you receive today as a sign of His glory?

saint.text: Jesus sanctified Baptism by being Himself baptized. If the Son of God was baptized, what godly man is he that despiseth Baptism?
saint.who: St. Cyril of Jerusalem, Catechetical Lectures

jan-13.q: Christ sanctified baptism by receiving it. How will you honour your own baptism today, perhaps with the sign of the cross and a prayer of thanks?

saint.text: For darkened affections is removal from Thee. For it is not by our feet, or change of place, that men leave Thee, or return unto Thee.

lent-1.q: We return to God by turning our hearts, not moving our feet. What one inner habit will you turn from this Lent, and what will you turn toward?

saint.text: As far as I can understand, the gate by which to enter this castle is prayer and meditation.
saint.who: St. Teresa of Avila, The Interior Castle

lent-2.q: Jesus says to go into your room and pray in secret. When and where will you keep a fixed quiet time with Him this week?

saint.text: It therefore belongs to a virtuous life to show mercy and to fast in secret; that thou mayest seem to be seeking a reward from thy God alone, and not from men.
saint.who: St. Ambrose, On the Duties of the Clergy

lent-3.q: Fasting is joined to mercy and kept hidden. What will you give up quietly this week, and who will receive what you save?

saint.text: Lend unto Him who wants nothing, yet hath need for thy sake; who feeds all men, yet is an hungered, that thou mayest not suffer famine; who is poor, that thou mayest be rich.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew

lent-4.q: Christ is poor so that you may be rich. Whom will you help this week, trusting that you are lending to Him?

saint.text: For who, that is set in the uncertainty of this life, can be found either exempt from temptation, or free from fault?
saint.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on Lent

lent-5.q: Even Jesus was tempted in the desert. Which temptation returns to you most often, and what is your plan for the moment it comes?

saint.text: It remains, therefore, that we should understand the daily bread as spiritual, that is to say, divine precepts, which we ought daily to meditate and to labour after.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Our Lord’s Sermon on the Mount

lent-6.q: Man lives by every word from God. What passage of Scripture will you read and keep with you each day this week?

saint.text: For as soon as He had said to him, “Get thee hence,” He caused him to take to flight; since he brought not against Him any other temptations.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew

lent-7.q: Jesus answered the tempter with a single firm word and the tempter left. What short, firm answer will you give when your own temptation comes?

saint.text: And in this Transfiguration the foremost object was to remove the offence of the cross from the disciple’s heart, and to prevent their faith being disturbed by the humiliation of His voluntary Passion by revealing to them the excellence of His hidden dignity.
saint.who: St. Leo the Great, Homily on the Transfiguration

lent-8.q: Jesus showed His glory to prepare His friends for the cross. What hard thing ahead can you face by recalling a moment God has shown Himself to you?

saint.text: And what saith the voice? “This is my beloved Son.” Now if He is beloved, fear not thou, O Peter.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew

lent-9.q: The Father says, “Listen to him.” What command of Jesus have you been avoiding, and what small step will you take on it today?

saint.text: But what other counsel is there than this, that he who desires to have divine help for his own infirmity should bear that of others, and should assist it as much as possible?
saint.who: St. Augustine, Our Lord’s Sermon on the Mount

lent-10.q: We receive God’s mercy as we bear with others’ weakness. Whose faults will you carry patiently today instead of correcting or avoiding them?

saint.text: For in no other sentence do we pray in such a way that we, as it were, enter into a compact with God: for we say, “Forgive us, as we also forgive.” And if we lie in that compact, the whole prayer is fruitless.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Our Lord’s Sermon on the Mount

lent-11.q: Every time you pray the Our Father, you make a promise to forgive. Whom do you need to forgive, and what will you do about it this week?

saint.text: Let us remit, that we may have remission: let us grant the pardon which we crave: let us not be eager to be revenged when we pray to be forgiven.
saint.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on Lent

lent-12.q: Peter asked how often to forgive. Which old grievance will you set down this week, rather than saving it to bring up again?

saint.text: Nothing else, however elevated, perfects the soul which must never seek to forget its own nothingness. Let humility be always at work, like the bee at the honeycomb, or all will be lost.
saint.who: St. Teresa of Avila, The Interior Castle

lent-13.q: The tax collector asked only for mercy and went home justified. Where can you stop defending yourself and simply tell God the truth about yourself?

saint.text: That He may heal us, let us take His yoke upon us, and learn of Him who is meek and lowly in heart, and we shall find rest unto our souls: for His yoke is easy, and His burden is light.

lent-14.q: Jesus invites you to learn from Him, gentle and lowly. What burden of pride or worry could you set down in order to take up His yoke?

saint.text: Because thou hast eyes to see the heavens: a heart thou hast not yet to see the Maker of heaven: therefore came He from heaven to earth, to cleanse the heart, that He may be seen who made heaven and earth.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Expositions on the Psalms

lent-15.q: Only a clean heart can see God, and He heals patiently. What wound will you let Him treat, even if it is uncomfortable?

saint.text: For it is not so much the corruptible flesh as the clean heart, which is made a shrine for God, and a temple of the Holy Ghost.

lent-16.q: God makes His dwelling in a clean heart, not in outward show. What one thing needs cleaning out of your heart before Easter?

saint.text: And so, dearly-beloved, if we unhesitatingly believe with the heart what we profess with the mouth, in Christ we are crucified, we are dead, we are buried; on the very third day, too, we are raised.
saint.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on the Lord’s Resurrection

easter-1.q: Which grudge or habit, buried with Christ, will you leave in the tomb today instead of carrying it with you into the Easter season?

saint.text: But the hour had now come when the joy, in some measure announced by the angels, who forbade her tears, was to succeed the weeping.

easter-2.q: What sorrow are you still weeping over? Listen for Christ calling your name today, and place that one grief in his hands.

saint.text: For they saw that He was dead, and they had no hope that He would rise again; all their hope was gone.

easter-3.q: Where has your hope gone quiet, as though it were over? Tell Jesus plainly today what you had hoped for, as the two on the road did.

saint.text: Yes, for a word from the divine Scriptures, made to sound in the ear, doth more than fire soften the hardened soul, and renders it fit for all good things.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew

easter-4.q: When did Scripture last warm your heart? Give ten minutes today to one Gospel passage, reading slowly until a single word stays with you.

saint.text: And He departed from our eyes, that we might return into our heart, and there find Him.

easter-5.q: Christ vanishes from sight so that we may find him within. Where will you stop today, in silence, to look for him in your own heart?

saint.text: For nails had pierced His hands, a spear had laid open His side: and there the marks of the wounds are preserved for healing the hearts of the doubting.

easter-6.q: Which of your own wounds could Christ’s wounds heal? Bring it honestly to him today, and pray Thomas’s words: “My Lord and my God.”

saint.text: Forego vengeance, forgive offences: exchange severity for gentleness, indignation for meekness, discord for peace.
saint.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on Lent

easter-7.q: Whose peace have you been withholding? Choose one offence to forgive or one discord to soften today, and give Christ’s greeting a concrete word or act.

saint.text: Believers know the body of Christ, if they neglect not to be the body of Christ.

easter-8.q: After receiving Christ in the Eucharist, how will you become what you received? Name one way you will be bread for someone this week.

saint.text: An hundred and fifty fishes were taken—by Simon’s net from the water;—but there were taken by his preaching,—out of the bosom of Baptism,—ten thousands and thousands of men,—a draught of the sons of the Kingdom.
saint.who: St. Ephrem the Syrian, Hymns for the Epiphany

easter-9.q: Where have you worked all night and caught nothing? Hand that task to Christ today, and try one thing at his word.

saint.text: He also forthwith forgave Peter, for he wept most bitterly. And if you weep bitterly Christ will look upon you and your guilt shall leave you.

easter-10.q: Where have you failed Christ as Peter did? Bring that failure to him in honest tears today, expecting forgiveness rather than reproach.

saint.text: If, then, the care of feeding is the proof of loving, whosoever abounds in virtues, and yet refuses to feed the flock of God, is convicted of not loving the chief Shepherd.
saint.who: St. Gregory the Great, Pastoral Rule

easter-11.q: Christ asks you what he asked Peter: do you love me? Answer him this week by feeding someone with your time, patience, or practical help.

saint.text: He hath brought me forth in the narrow ways, wherein few walk, of His righteousness; not for my merit’s sake, but for His Name’s sake.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Expositions on the Psalms

easter-12.q: Which narrow way is the Shepherd leading you through now? Name it, and follow him one step today rather than choosing the easier path.

saint.text: And whither go we, but to Him, and by what way go we, but by Him?

easter-13.q: Where are you trying to reach God by some other road? Take one decision today and ask what going by Christ himself would look like.

saint.text: Seest thou that the love of God is intertwined with our own, and connected like a sort of chain?
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on John

easter-14.q: Whose love has been a link in the chain that holds you to God? Return it today by loving one person in a concrete way.

saint.text: For when the branch is cut off, another may spring up from the living root; but that which is cut off cannot live apart from the root.

easter-15.q: What has cut you off from the root: neglected prayer, resentment, busyness? Choose one thing to reconnect you with Christ this week, and begin today.

saint.text: And He is called the Comforter, because He comforts and encourages us, and helpeth our infirmities
saint.who: St. Cyril of Jerusalem, Catechetical Lectures

easter-16.q: In which weakness do you most need the Comforter? Pray “Come, Holy Spirit” today, and ask for his help in that one place.

saint.text: He that will have joy of himself shall be sad; but he that will have his joy of God will ever rejoice, because God is everlasting.

easter-17.q: Where are you seeking a joy that cannot last? Place your joy in God today by thanking him for three gifts no one can take away.

saint.text: We bless the Lord our God, who gathered us together to spiritual joy. Let us be ever in humility of heart, and let our joy be with Him.

easter-18.q: With whom could you share this Easter joy? Make a call or share a meal with one person today, and give thanks together.

saint.text: So ought we also to rejoice, who have been thought worthy to know the Son of God; to rejoice, not in thought alone, but to show it also by our actions.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on John

easter-19.q: How could you show your joy in Christ by action today, not only by feeling? Choose one deed of obedience or kindness, and do it gladly.

saint.text: Let joy be wholly of hope to come, desire be wholly of eternal life. Let all sighings breathe after Christ.

easter-20.q: What do you long for that only eternal life can satisfy? Pray today for that full joy, and set aside one small thing that dims it.

saint.text: For indeed the preacher drinks out of his own cistern, when, returning to his own heart, he first listens himself to what he has to say.
saint.who: St. Gregory the Great, Pastoral Rule

easter-21.q: Before you speak of Christ to anyone, which word do you most need to hear yourself? Listen to it in prayer, then share it with one person.

saint.text: He who speaks to you in person has what He has not left, and yet He came; for by coming He departed not thence, nor has He forsaken us by returning thither.

easter-22.q: Where do you most need to remember that Christ has not left you? Say “You are with me” before one hard task today.

saint.text: For then He sent the Holy Ghost: by whom the disciples being fulfilled preached with confidence the Word of God, that Churches might be collected.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Expositions on the Psalms

easter-23.q: The Spirit gives courage to witness. Where could you speak or act as a disciple this week with a boldness you usually lack?

saint.text: And so, dearly-beloved, let us rejoice with spiritual joy, and let us with gladness pay God worthy thanks and raise our hearts’ eyes unimpeded to those heights where Christ is.
saint.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on the Lord’s Ascension

easter-24.q: As Christ is lifted up, which earthly worry will you set down? Spend a quiet minute today looking toward him with thanks.

saint.text: Let us not then be taken up with the appearances of temporal matters, neither let our contemplations be diverted from heavenly to earthly things.
saint.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on the Lord’s Resurrection

easter-25.q: Which temporal concern keeps pulling your thoughts downward? Choose a moment today to turn toward heaven on purpose, and let one anxiety rest.

saint.text: Because there are many at this time who say that they fear and love God, but in their works show the contrary; but God requireth that love which is shown by works.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on John

easter-26.q: Where does your love for Christ currently live only in words? Choose one concrete act of obedience to do today.

saint.text: That we should establish ourselves in a sense of God’s Presence, by continually conversing with Him.
saint.who: Brother Lawrence, The Practice of the Presence of God

easter-27.q: Christ promises not to leave you orphaned. At what moment today could you simply turn and speak to him?

saint.text: Peace He leaveth with us, that here also we may love one another: His own peace will He give us, where we shall be beyond the possibility of dissension.

easter-28.q: Whose quarrel is keeping your peace from being shared? Name one person you will make a first move toward today.

saint.text: For although, when the branch beareth little fruit, the husbandman purgeth it that it may bring forth more; yet if it abide not in the vine, and draw its life from the root, it can bear no fruit whatever of itself.

easter-29.q: Where are you trying to bear fruit on your own strength? Set aside ten quiet minutes today to draw from the root.

saint.text: It is not, then, for the purpose of awakening His love to us that we first keep His commandments; but this, that unless He loves us, we cannot keep His commandments.

easter-30.q: If his love comes first, what burden of earning it can you lay down today, and obey from gratitude instead?

saint.text: Ye see, beloved, how great and wonderful a thing is love, and that there is no declaring its perfection.
saint.who: St. Clement of Rome, First Letter to the Corinthians

easter-31.q: Who in your life needs to be loved as Christ has loved you? Decide one costly way to show it this week.

saint.text: We are therefore to understand that he who loves has already the Holy Spirit, and by what he has becomes worthy of a fuller possession, that by having the more he may love the more.

easter-32.q: Where do you already sense the Spirit's presence in your love? Ask today for a fuller measure, and name what you will do with it.

saint.text: The Spirit is a gift of God, but a gift of life, for the law of “the Spirit of life,” it is said, “hath made” us “free;”
saint.who: St. Basil the Great, On the Holy Spirit

easter-33.q: What in you still feels bound or lifeless? Ask the Spirit to teach and free you there, and listen for his answer.

saint.text: For not even to His elect in this life has He promised the joys of delight, but the bitternesses of tribulation; so that, after the manner of medicine, they may be restored through a bitter cup to the sweetness of eternal salvation.

easter-34.q: What current trouble could you carry today as something Christ has already overcome? Bring it to him in prayer by name.

saint.text: It is the same thing, therefore, that He now also prayed for in our behalf, as He did at that time in theirs, namely, that all—to wit, both we and they—may be one.

easter-35.q: Jesus prayed for your unity before you were born. Which division in your family, parish or workplace will you pray over today?

saint.text: It is profitable, therefore, that you should live in an unblameable unity, that thus ye may always enjoy communion with God.
saint.who: St. Ignatius of Antioch, Letter to the Ephesians

easter-36.q: What small habit of criticism or grumbling weakens the unity Christ prayed for? Replace it today with one word of encouragement.

saint.text: I could not be then, O my God, could not be at all, wert Thou not in me; or, rather, unless I were in Thee, of whom are all things, by whom are all things, in whom are all things?

easter-37.q: Christ in you and the Father in him: how does that change one thing you will say or do today?

saint.text: Thou awakest us to delight in Thy praise; for Thou madest us for Thyself, and our heart is restless, until it repose in Thee.

easter-38.q: Christ longs for you to be where he is. What restless pursuit might you set down today to rest in him?

saint.text: And so, dearly-beloved, let us rejoice with spiritual joy, and let us with gladness pay God worthy thanks and raise our hearts’ eyes unimpeded to those heights where Christ is.
saint.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on the Lord's Ascension

easter-39.q: Tomorrow we remember the Lord's ascension. What one earthly worry can you consciously lift up to Christ this evening?

saint.text: Since then Christ’s Ascension is our uplifting, and the hope of the Body is raised, whither the glory of the Head has gone before, let us exult, dearly-beloved, with worthy joy and delight in the loyal paying of thanks.
saint.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on the Lord's Ascension

easter-40.q: Where Christ the Head has gone, his Body follows. How will you let that hope shape one decision today?

saint.text: We have learnt from the Apostle, “the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and into the patient waiting for Christ”
saint.who: St. Basil the Great, On the Holy Spirit

easter-41.q: Waiting with Christ's promise is an act of love, not idleness. Where are you being asked to wait, and how will you wait well?

saint.text: For the Spirit made them men of iron instead of men of clay, gave them wings, and allowed them to be cast down by nothing human.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on John

easter-42.q: Where do you feel like clay, afraid to witness to Christ? Ask for the Spirit's strength before you speak or act today.

saint.text: Hence it is with justice and truth that we call the holy Mary the Mother of God. For this name embraces the whole mystery of the dispensation.
saint.who: St. John of Damascus, On the Orthodox Faith

easter-43.q: Mary waits with the disciples as Mother of the Lord. Ask for her prayers today for someone you are waiting alongside.

saint.text: being come together into the same place, let there be one prayer, one supplication, one mind, one hope, in love and in joy undefiled.
saint.who: St. Ignatius of Antioch, Letter to the Magnesians

easter-44.q: Who could you pray with today, even briefly, in person or by phone, as the disciples prayed together in the upper room?

saint.text: For it is the strength of great minds and the light of firmly-faithful souls, unhesitatingly to believe what is not seen with the bodily sight, and there to fix one’s affections whither you cannot direct your gaze.
saint.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on the Lord's Ascension

easter-45.q: What are you waiting for that you cannot yet see? Take one step today that trusts the promise rather than the outcome.

saint.text: For my part I keep myself retired with Him in the depth of centre of my soul as much as I can; and while I am so with Him I fear nothing; but the least turning from Him is insupportable.
saint.who: Brother Lawrence, The Practice of the Presence of God

easter-46.q: When can you give God five wordless minutes today, with your phone silent? Choose the time now and keep it.

saint.text: And when Thou art poured out on us, Thou art not cast down, but Thou upliftest us; Thou art not dissipated, but Thou gatherest us.

easter-47.q: God promises to pour out his Spirit. What would you ask him to gather and lift in you, or in your household?

saint.text: He came to thee in the flesh, that He might bedew thy thirsty lips: He will satisfy thee trusting, who bedewed thee thirsting.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Expositions on the Psalms

easter-48.q: What are you thirsting for that you keep seeking elsewhere? Bring that thirst to Christ in prayer today.

saint.text: Mistress of all good things is charity, which savours of nothing extraneous, nothing rough, nothing confused; which so exercises and strengthens hearts that nothing is heavy, nothing difficult, but all that is done becomes sweet.

easter-49.q: On the eve of Pentecost, which heavy task could love make lighter? Ask the Spirit to pour that love into your heart tonight.

saint.text: For the Spirit of Truth Himself makes the house of His glory shine with the brightness of His light, and will have nothing dark nor lukewarm in His temple.
saint.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on Whitsuntide

easter-50.q: What dark or lukewarm corner of your life will you open to the Spirit today, so that his fire can reach it?

saint.text: So then by our faith in Him He has made our love to God and our neighbour to grow, making us godly and righteous and good.
saint.who: St. Irenaeus, Demonstration of the Apostolic Preaching

lent-17.q: Which small, concrete act of love toward God or neighbor will you do this week to let your love grow, rather than merely hoping it will?

saint.text: For whosoever superintends the healing of wounds must needs administer in wine the smart of pain, and in oil the softness of loving-kindness, to the end that through wine what is festering may be purged, and through oil what is curable may be soothed.
saint.who: St. Gregory the Great, Pastoral Rule

lent-18.q: Whose wound near you needs both firmness and gentleness from you today, and what is one way you can tend it rather than walk past?

saint.text: God is all this to thee: if thou hungerest, He is bread to thee; if thou thirstest, He is water to thee; if thou art in darkness, He is light to thee: for He remains incorruptible.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John

lent-19.q: Where in your life are you walking in darkness, and what would it mean today to let Christ be the light you walk by?

saint.text: But because “the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us,” by His very nativity he made an eye-salve to cleanse the eyes of our heart, and to enable us to see His majesty by means of His humility.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John

lent-20.q: What can you see now, through Christ's humility, that you could not see at the start of Lent, and how will you act on it?

saint.text: If we thirst, let us come; and not by our feet, but by our affections; let us come, not by removing from our place, but by loving.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John

lent-21.q: What are you truly thirsting for today, and what would it mean to come to Christ by loving someone rather than by going anywhere?

saint.text: But He who was asking drink was thirsting for the faith of the woman herself.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John

lent-22.q: Christ asks you for a drink of faith. What small, honest offering of trust can you give Him today?

saint.text: There is, indeed, this resurrection which comes to pass now; unbelievers were dead, the unrighteous were dead; the righteous live, they pass from the death of unbelief to the life of faith.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John

lent-23.q: Where have you passed, or still need to pass, from unbelief to faith, and whom can you welcome back to life alongside you?

saint.text: Let us remit, that we may have remission: let us grant the pardon which we crave: let us not be eager to be revenged when we pray to be forgiven.

lent-24.q: Who owes you an apology you are still waiting for, and what pardon will you grant today before you ask to be forgiven?

saint.text: We pray with closed doors when with closed lips and complete silence we pray to the searcher not of words but of hearts.

lent-25.q: If God listens to the heart rather than to words, what could you leave unsaid and simply offer Him in ten silent minutes today?

saint.text: Let those who wish Christ to spare them, have mercy on the poor; let them give freely to feed the wretched, who desire to attain to the society of the blessed.

lent-26.q: Whom among the poor can you feed this week, and what will you give up in order to do it?

saint.text: The Fast should not end with abstinence from food, but lead to good deeds.

lent-27.q: Beyond what you are giving up, what good deed will your fast become today, and for whom?

saint.text: Observe how He leadeth her mind upward; for to raise Lazarus was not the only thing sought; it was necessary that both she and they who were with her should learn the Resurrection.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on John

lent-28.q: What is one tomb in your life, a habit or a grief, where you can trust that Christ gives life now, not only on the last day?

saint.text: Therefore He said not, “Let him renounce himself unto death,” but, “Let him take up his cross;” setting forth the reproachful death; and that not once, nor twice, but throughout all life one ought so to do.
saint.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew

lent-29.q: Where is Christ asking you to deny yourself not once but daily, and what is one concrete way you will carry that cross today?

saint.text: But the height of His glorification had to be preceded by the depth of His passion.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John

lent-30.q: What must fall into the ground and die in you, a comfort or a grudge, so that fruit can come before Easter?

saint.text: Consequently, that the cause of all diseases might be cured, namely, pride, the Son of God came down and was made low.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John

lent-31.q: Where does pride keep you from stepping lower this week, and what lowly act of service can you offer in imitation of Christ?

saint.text: Sometimes I consider myself there, as a stone before a carver, whereof he is to make a statue: presenting myself thus before God, I desire Him to make His perfect image in my soul, and render me entirely like Himself.
saint.who: Brother Lawrence, The Practice of the Presence of God

lent-32.q: What in your heart would you ask God to carve away, and will you sit still before Him for five minutes to let Him begin?

saint.text: Let all men’s faith then be established, according to the preaching of the most holy Gospel, and let no one be ashamed of Christ’s cross, through which the world was redeemed.

lent-33.q: Where are you tempted to be ashamed of Christ or of the cross, and how can you quietly acknowledge Him there this week?

saint.text: That same Jesus Christ our Lord, that same Jesus exactly, He is the complete Physician of our wounds.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John

lent-34.q: Which of your wounds, hidden or obvious, have you not yet brought to the Physician who bore His own for you? Bring one today.

saint.text: And the cause of our restoration is naught else but the mercy of God, Whom we should not have loved, unless He had first loved us, and dispelled the darkness of our ignorance by the light of His truth.

lent-35.q: Whose love first reached you before you deserved it, and how can you love someone first today, without waiting to be loved?

saint.text: What moves You to do us such mercy through pure love, and on account of no debt that You owed us, or need that You had of us?
saint.who: St. Catherine of Siena, The Dialogue

lent-36.q: God owed you nothing, yet gave everything. To whom can you show unearned kindness today, someone you owe nothing at all?

saint.text: I seek the bread of God, which is the flesh of Jesus Christ; and I seek His blood, a drink which is love incorruptible.
saint.who: St. Ignatius of Antioch, Letter to the Romans

lent-37.q: What hunger in you has been feeding on lesser things, and how will you let Christ be the bread you truly seek today?

saint.text: This is the reason for the sojourn of Christ in the flesh, the pattern life described in the Gospels, the sufferings, the cross, the tomb, the resurrection; so that the man who is being saved through imitation of Christ receives that old adoption.
saint.who: St. Basil the Great, On the Holy Spirit

lent-38.q: Which step of Christ's way, from His sufferings to the cross and the tomb, are you being asked to imitate this week, and how?

saint.text: For that which was and is a reproach to Him, and for His sake to us, even the cross, this same is, says he, His government, being a sign of His kingdom.
saint.who: St. Irenaeus, Demonstration of the Apostolic Preaching

lent-39.q: The cross, once a reproach, is Christ's sign of kingship. What reproach or humiliation might you accept today as a way of following your King?

saint.text: The branches of palm trees are laudatory emblems, significant of victory, because the Lord was about to overcome death by dying, and by the trophy of His cross to triumph over the devil, the prince of death.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John

lent-40.q: The crowd waved palms for a King who would conquer by dying. How will you welcome Him this week, even when it costs you?

saint.text: Helpless, I cast myself at the feet of Jesus, I watered them with my tears, I wiped them with my hair: and then I subdued my rebellious body with weeks of abstinence.

lent-41.q: Mary poured out something precious at Jesus' feet. What precious thing, time, money, or pride, will you pour out for Him today?

saint.text: The Lord Jesus declares that He is giving His disciples a new commandment, that they should love one another.
saint.who: St. Augustine, Tractates on the Gospel of John

lent-42.q: Which person is hardest for you to love as Christ has loved you, and what is one concrete act of love toward them today?

saint.text: Return to thy right mind; lay aside thy madness and be wise. Mercy invites thee, Salvation knocks at the door, Life recalls thee to life.

lent-43.q: Christ keeps calling even the one about to betray Him. Where are you resisting His patient mercy, and what would returning to your right mind look like?

saint.text: Judge not the matter from the taste, but from faith be fully assured without misgiving, that the Body and Blood of Christ have been vouchsafed to thee.
saint.who: St. Cyril of Jerusalem, Mystagogic Catecheses

lent-44.q: Tonight, how will you meet Christ in the Eucharist by faith rather than by feeling, and whom will you then serve as He served?

saint.text: Among all the works of God’s mercy, dearly-beloved, which from the beginning have been bestowed upon men’s salvation, none is more wondrous, and none more sublime, than that Christ was crucified for the world.

lent-45.q: Christ was crucified for the world, and for you. In silence before the cross today, what do you want to say to Him?

saint.text: A medicine of life has entered into Hell, and has restored life to its dead.
saint.who: St. Ephrem the Syrian, Nisibene Hymns

lent-46.q: Christ is at work even in the silence of the tomb. Where are you waiting today, and can you wait there in trust?
